scope: Official-primary-source currentness research for the controlled-pleading records in the literal remaining-39 partition. This file does not adopt law, enable a route, or replace counsel review.

records.issuingBody: Council of the District of Columbia, D.C. Law Library
sourceText: D.C. Code section 24-906(e-1) permits a youth offender, after the later completion event specified there, to move for a discretionary set-aside; section 24-906(e-1)(2) directs the court to the factors in section 24-903(c)(2) and requires reasons on the record.
inference: The operative statute and factors are now pinned. This pass did not establish whether a standing form or chamber practice exists.
Service, response practice, motion sequence, and the relationship between set-aside and later sealing still require a court-practice survey or counsel determination.
remainingEvidence: Current Superior Court standing practice or form confirmation
Service and response rules for a section 24-906(e-1) motion

sourceText: The current official section 19-2604 text identifies application-based discretionary dismissal/set-aside and felony-reduction routes, their required showings, the five-year/prosecutor-stipulation conditions for specified reductions, and the sex-offender-registration exclusion. It does not prescribe a statewide application form in the saved text.

The current official section 67-3004 text separately permits a written request to the department and sealing of the official court file for specified noncharge, acquittal, and dismissal outcomes, while expressly excluding a dismissal under section 19-2604(1) from that provision.

The Idaho Supreme Court's current treatment-court rules place treatment-court orders and completion records in the clerk-maintained criminal case file, while the treatment-court coordinator separately maintains participant applications. The rules provide a statewide procedural framework while allowing approved local rules.
The operative Idaho Legislature pages are now saved and hash-pinned under the Codex source-receipt path.
inference: The treatment-court rules do not supply a statewide post-completion reduction or dismissal motion form.

Current statutory text is no longer the source gap. A complete statewide/county vehicle survey remains necessary before caption, attachments, service, proposed-order practice, fee, or local variation can be treated as current.
remainingEvidence: Statewide form search plus county-by-county vehicle exceptions
Complete pleading elements, service, fee, venue, and order practice

sourceText: NRS 179.271 uses a written request to the court of conviction, prosecutor notice, a ten-judicial-day objection window, a hearing if there is an objection, and no fee; it excludes violations of traffic laws.

NRS 179.273 directs automatic sealing when the court and Central Repository receive a certified unconditional pardon, while also allowing the person to petition the convicting court with proof; that petition does not go through prosecutor review and carries no fee.
NRS 179A.160 uses written applications to the Central Repository and each maintaining agency after a favorable disposition, subject to the disqualifying conditions stated in that section.
inference: The decriminalization and pardon routes have current operative text sufficient for a canonical owner to draft and review their vehicle; this lane has not decided any form or local-rule requirement.

Repository removal is agency correspondence, not a court pleading. A candidate participant treatment can state the actor and destination while deferring any unverified prescribed application contents.
remainingEvidence: Counsel-approved form and local-rule determination for NRS 179.271 and 179.273
Agency-confirmed application contents or an exact no-prescribed-form treatment for NRS 179A.160

records.issuingBody: South Carolina General Assembly; South Carolina Judicial Branch
sourceText: The current South Carolina Judicial Branch inventory publishes the SCCA 223A1, 223A1(a), 223B1, 223C1, 223C1(a), and 223D1 expungement form family; the official SCCA 223A1 PDF is marked Revised 04/2026.
The official bytes for the complete identified 223 family were saved without altering the existing pleading configurations.

The current official Code text now pins sections 17-22-350 and 17-22-550: the traffic-education provision states its application and participation fee rules and inability-to-pay waiver; the alcohol-education provision states its enrollment fee, possible provider fees, and discretionary waiver or reduction.

Sections 17-22-910 through 17-22-940 place the covered expungement process with the circuit solicitor, require the appropriate blank expungement order form from the circuit solicitor to the exclusion of other expungement forms, and state the administrative, SLED-verification, clerk-fee, single-incident, and program-specific fee rules.

SCCA 223B1 expressly identifies the Traffic Education Program under section 17-22-330(A) and the Alcohol Education Program under section 17-22-530(A); SCCA 223A1 expressly identifies conditional discharge under section 44-53-450(B).
inference: The saved forms resolve the track-to-form mapping: SCCA 223B1 maps the TEP and AEP tracks, and SCCA 223A1 maps the conditional-discharge track. That does not resolve the recorded fee conflict or provide reviewed field maps.

The previously unread section 17-22-350 and 17-22-550 text is no longer a source gap. The canonical owner must reconcile each track's exact section 17-22-940 fee/exemption treatment with the official form path rather than copy a single fee across all three tracks.
Field maps, current statutory fit, visual review, and counsel adoption remain mandatory before any participant packet can be exposed.
remainingEvidence: Track-specific application of sections 17-22-350, 17-22-550, and 17-22-940 and resolution of the recorded fee conflict
Reviewed field maps, rendered fixtures, and counsel adoption

records.issuingBody: Virginia General Assembly; Supreme Court of Virginia
sourceText: The official DC-363 instructions expressly identify Virginia Code section 19.2-392.2(B), when another person used the petitioner's name or identifying information, and section 19.2-392.2(H), when an arrest or charge resulted from mistaken identity or unauthorized use of identifying information.

The current official DC-363 form itself contains separate subsection-B and subsection-H selections, the charge/disposition/court fields, charging-document attachment, fingerprint statement, signature, and clerk-or-notary acknowledgment.

The official Virginia Code page contains both the version effective through November 30, 2026 and the version effective December 1, 2026. Both preserve the subsection-B identity-use petition and subsection-H mistaken-person motion, fingerprint requirement, and subsection-K order handling relevant to DC-363.
inference: The prior dependency on a survey for a subsection-B/H vehicle is resolved in the Codex evidence lane: DC-363 is an official vehicle for both stated grounds.

The effective-date reconciliation is also resolved for the route's core B/H vehicle, but the canonical owner still must ingest these sources, bind fields without extending the form, and obtain technical and legal review.
remainingEvidence: Canonical field map, fixtures, and review

records.issuingBody: Washington State Legislature; Washington State Administrative Office of the Courts
sourceText: The official Washington forms index currently lists CRO 01.0100, 01.0200, 01.0300, 01.0600, and 01.0700 as the Certificate of Restoration of Opportunity petition, notice, proof of service, dismissal order, and certificate/order set.
The same inventory cautions that local superior-court rules may require additional documents.

RCW 9.97.020(11) requires the Administrative Office of the Courts to prepare instructions, forms, and a brochure; the statute calls for a sample standard application and form order and requires distribution and updates.
inference: The five-form source gap is closed in this candidate lane. The statute's word sample weighs against treating the AOC set as a universally mandatory form, but it does not decide which documents a particular court requires or eliminate local additions.
A canonical owner must document the pattern-form decision, survey exact local additions for the filing venue, create field maps, and obtain review.
remainingEvidence: Counsel-approved pattern-form decision grounded in RCW 9.97.020(11)
Exact local superior-court additions for the participant's filing venue and the statutory exemption screen
Canonical field maps, fixtures, legal adoption, and staging acceptance

sourceText: The current official section 973.015(1m)(b) text states that after successful completion of the sentence, the detaining or probationary authority issues a certificate of discharge that is forwarded to the court of record and has the effect of expunging the record.

The official Wisconsin Supreme Court opinion confirms that the sentencing court's expunction directive operates through the detaining or probationary authority's certificate process after successful completion, rather than through a new merits petition drafted by the participant.

The current official CR-266 form is expressly titled and limited to non-probation/non-incarceration cases. It is not a general substitute for a missing certificate from a detaining or probationary authority on this track.
inference: The existing record is in the wrong implementation family: participant correspondence and an exact no-response deferral are appropriate candidates, not a court pleading.

The candidate correspondence must avoid promising a remedy or deadline that the official sources do not establish for this certificate-follow-up track; current CR-266 must not be presented as a universal fallback.
remainingEvidence: Canonical participant-correspondence adoption and a counsel-reviewed determination of any case-specific non-response remedy
